name: Surface Splatting and Lighting

# Surface Splatting and Lighting
## Overview
Surface Splatting and Lighting is a family of rendering techniques that reconstruct continuous, shaded surfaces from unstructured point cloud samples by projecting each point as a spatially extended primitive (a splat) carrying a reconstruction kernel [G]. It solves the problem of sparse dot cloud aliasing and transparency artifacts inherent in raw [point rendering](#2827-point-based-rendering.md) by ensuring hole-free reconstructions even for moderate sampling densities [G]. Unlike forward [splatting](#23-splatting.md) methods that apply lighting during [rasterization](#15310-rasterization.md), variants like [Deferred Surface Splatting](1072-deferred-surface-splatting.md) decouple geometric projection from lighting calculation, allowing multiple light sources to be applied efficiently in screen space without re-projecting geometry [G].
## Shared principles
The family operates on a set of point cloud samples $P = \{p_i\}$, where each sample $p_i$ has a position $\mathbf{p}$, a color $\mathbf{c}$, and optionally a normal $\mathbf{n}$ [G]. Each sample is converted into a splat $S_j$ defined by a center $c_j$, tangent vectors $\mathbf{u}_j, \mathbf{v}_j$, and radii $r_u, r_v$ [G]. The rendering process generally involves: (1) transforming the object-space splat into screen space, (2) rasterizing the splat footprint as a low-pass filter to suppress aliasing, (3) accumulating overlapping contributions by computing a distance-based weight $w$ and additively blending attributes (color, normal, depth), and (4) computing illumination either per-splat or in a final screen-space pass [G].
## Subtopics

### [Deferred Surface Splatting](1072-deferred-surface-splatting.md)
Converts point clouds into continuous surfaces using a [deferred pipeline](#12306-deferred-shading-with-alpha-blended-feature-maps.md) with a G-buffer. It decouples projection from lighting, allowing efficient multi-light support in screen space. Choose this when multiple lights or complex shading models are required without re-projecting geometry.

### [Phong Splatting](2802-phong-splatting.md)
Assigns a linearly varying normal field to each elliptical splat, enabling per-pixel Phong shading. It is projectively correct and solves piecewise constant shading artifacts. Choose this for high-quality, physically-based shading of point clouds with fewer primitives than triangle meshes.

### [EWA Surface Splatting](8199-ewa-surface-splatting.md)
Uses band-limited reconstruction kernels ([surface splats](#2802-phong-splatting.md)) to efficiently suppress aliasing and guarantee hole-free reconstructions under [arbitrary transformations](#8412-arbitrary-permutation-transformations-for-svdag.md). It builds on [Surface Splatting and Lighting](9275-surface-splatting-and-lighting.md) and is chosen for high-quality, band-limited rendering of dense point clouds.

## Background
Surface splatting was introduced as a method to render point samples by superimposing band-limited reconstruction kernels in the image domain [G]. It efficiently suppresses aliasing artifacts and guarantees hole-free reconstructions even for moderate sampling densities [G]. The technique has been extended to support various [lighting models](#2056-lighting-models.md), including deferred shading and Phong shading, to address the visual quality limitations of simple point sprites [G].
